new.n: Romadka railroad extension grade and depot site, York sec. 10 (1880s-90s)
new.pl: Grade in York sec. 14, T25N R1W, about 1 km west-northwest of the mill; the line runs toward sec. 10, Clark County
new.v: Railroad spikes, tools, camp losses, coins
new.st: In fall 1883 the Romadka Bros. of Milwaukee bought about 4,500 acres in York and Fremont towns. They built the Romadka sawmill in York sec. 24, with a Milwaukee Road spur to Lynn that was being pulled up about 1923. A planned extension was graded as far as sec. 10 of York, where a 10-acre depot site was laid out. A local history says the frames of abandoned bridges "still stand concealed in the woods" (Romadka History, wiclarkcountyhistory.org). The 2018 USGS 1 m LiDAR shows a straight raised grade about 480 m long in sec. 14, running west-northwest from the mill toward sec. 10 (ends at 44.64319,-90.47128 and 44.64158,-90.46769), with higher fills at both ends where it crossed low ground. The pin is on the middle of that grade. Section 10 itself (centre 44.6619,-90.4864) shows no grade on the LiDAR, so the depot ground there is not placed yet.
new.t: Look for the straight grade and the bridge frames on the LiDAR, where an unbuilt rail grade shows as a raised line through the woods. Grading camps and the depot site are where the losses are. Ask the landowner.

pc-mill-york-sec-24.st: This was the Romadka sawmill. Romadka Bros. of Milwaukee bought about 4,500 acres in York and Fremont in fall 1883 and built the mill here, served by a Milwaukee Road spur to Lynn that was taken up about 1923 (Romadka History, wiclarkcountyhistory.org). Romadka was "the next station west" of Lynn in 1900.
